english.notes:
(i) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is NOT available in the magistrates court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence.
(ii) Section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 shall have effect as if the person to whom the property belongs or is treated as belonging for the purposes of the Criminal Damage Act 1971 were the victim of the offence.
(iii) If this offence is tried by a Crown Court, it is open to the jury to return a finding of guilt to the lesser charge of simple criminal damage. In R v Fennell (2000) the point was raised that if the damage was under £5000 the offence is treated as summary and the Crown Court have no jurisdiction. However, F was unsuccessful, the offence is still either way and the Crown Court can deal with such a matter.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
